135: He once was sleeping in a wharf;

137: And autumn winds begun to blow.
138: The angry surge beat on the wharf,
139: Nor ceased to dash against its steps;
143: He woke. But all was dark and dull;
144: The rain fell fast; the shrill blasts wailed

148: The horrors of the past, and rose,

152: The dreary space that stretched around.
154: He found himself beneath the porch
155: Of spacious house. And on the steps,
156: With upraised paws, as large as life,
157: Two lions stood, both keeping guard:

160: Sate, with his royal hand outstretched,
161: The giant on his steed of bronze.

168: He saw the lions, square, and him,

171: As ever, with his hand outstretched,
172: He watched the city he had built.
173: The poor mad creature wildly roamed
174: Around the rock with aching limbs.
